minor.issue: test_iter51_deploy_guard_and_alerts.py::test_alert_cooldown_prevents_spam intermittently returns 0 alerts (expected 1) when run via the FastAPI-scheduled subprocess (elapsed ~103s under load). The same suite passes cleanly and consistently when invoked directly via bash /app/backend/scripts/run_regression.sh (exit 0, 10/10 iter51 tests). Not a code regression from iter53b; appears to be a timing/ordering flake specific to the async subprocess runner. Consequence: /api/auth/health can show status=fail after an auto-run even though the source-of-truth bash regression is green.

action_items: Investigate the flaky iter51 test_alert_cooldown_prevents_spam when triggered via /api/admin/deploy-readiness/run-now (async subprocess) — consider serialising alerts collection writes or adding an explicit poll for the alert row instead of a fixed sleep(2). Bash-invoked regression is stable.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py continues to grow (900+ lines with lifespan/on_event mix, regression-guard scheduler, save-health alert engine, alert-types persistence all in one module). Suggest extracting into /app/backend/routers/admin_ops.py (deploy-readiness + save-health-alerts) and /app/backend/services/regression_guard.py.

run_regression.sh runs each test file sequentially via a fresh pytest invocation — startup cost multiplied 13x. Consider a single pytest invocation with a marker/deselect for known slow files; current wall-clock ~100s per API-triggered run is why alert-cooldown timing flakes.
server.py:307 /api/admin/deploy-readiness/run-now returns 'triggered' even when a run is already in-flight — no debounce/lock exposed. Rapid re-clicks from UI could stack subprocesses.

Iter53b test test_save_failure_disabled_suppresses_alert deletes the entire save_health_alerts collection at setup, which can wipe alerts from a concurrent run of iter51 tests when they execute in parallel/adjacent order. Consider scoping the delete by a marker field.
